svg.text: Everyday English - Grammar
Inversion after Not only
MEANING
When Not only begins a clause for emphasis,
put the auxiliary before the subject.
IN CONTEXT
Not only did she finish early, but she also
helped the rest of the team.
USAGE NOTE
Pattern: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb.
Without an existing auxiliary, use do/does/did +
base verb. Ordinary order remains in She not
only finished early but also helped us.
CONVERSATION
A: Was the workshop useful?
B: Not only did I learn new skills, but I also met
people in my field.
A: Why did you put did before I?
B: Starting with Not only requires inversion;
learn stays in its base form.
YOUR TURN
Rewrite: He saved us time and also improved
the design. Begin with Not only.
